title: Part II
author: David Hume
summary: Demea holds that the nature of God is beyond human understanding. Cleanthes replies with the argument from design: the world is a great machine, so its author must resemble the mind of man. Philo attacks the analogy: we have seen houses built, but never worlds, and thought is only one small agitation of the brain.

notes.note: Nicolas Malebranche (1638–1715), priest of the Oratory. Hume's note cites his *De la recherche de la vérité* (1674–75), book iii.
An early Christian sect who held that God has a human form.

The story is told by Cicero, *De natura deorum*, i. 60: asked by Hiero, tyrant of Syracuse, what God was, the poet Simonides kept doubling the time he needed, because the longer he thought, the more obscure the question seemed.

notes.on: Galilæo's famous Dialogues concerning the system of the world
notes.note: Galileo Galilei, *Dialogo sopra i due massimi sistemi del mondo* (1632).
